decision_conditions: <p data-pm-slice="1 1 []">The proposed change of use from a 6-bedroom, 6-person House in Multiple Occupation (Use Class C4) to a 7-bedroom, 7-person House in Multiple Occupation (sui generis) would fall outside the C4 use class, which is limited to small HMOs occupied by between three and six residents, and would fall within the sui generis category under the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (as amended). The proposed change of use would constitute a material change of use requiring planning permission.&nbsp; Furthermore, the proposed seventh bedroom relies on additional floorspace created by a loft dormer, which does not form part of the development for which the present certificate is sought. The applicant has failed to demonstrate that the proposed use is authorised by any applicable permitted development right or other statutory provision, and is not within the tolerances of&nbsp;<span style="color: rgb(51, 51, 51);">of Part 3 of Schedule 2 of The Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (as amended).&nbsp;</span></p><p>Accordingly, the applicant has failed to demonstrate, on the balance of probabilities, that the proposed use would be lawful. The application for a certificate of lawfulness proposed use or development is therefore refused under Section 192 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended).</p>
